records.text: A Horde Air Force Alarm Bot is a mechanical alarm device.
A Mo'arg Engineer works among the Legion's engineers and tinkerers at the Nagrand forge camps. Altruis says distracting them would slow work on the Legion structures while he devises an attack plan.
A Boulderfist ogre encountered around Nagrand’s Burning Blade Ruins, where Jorin Deadeye calls for the Mag’har to answer the ogres with force. The Crusher fights with Pulverize.
A Boulderfist ogre mystic in the Burning Blade Ruins, among those Jorin Deadeye wants the Mag'har to answer with force. It hurls lightning and Earth Shock and heals itself when hurt.

A Boulderfist shock troop hiding in Nagrand's Northwind and Southwind clefts, according to Jorin Deadeye, who wants those troops killed in the name of the Mag'har. The Warrior fights with two weapons.

A Boulderfist shock troop found in Nagrand's Northwind and Southwind clefts. Jorin Deadeye says these troops hide their ogre mounds there and wants those encountered killed in the name of the Mag'har. This Mage blasts foes with Fire Blast.

A Warmaul reaver serving with Zorbo the Advisor’s forces in Nagrand’s Laughing Skull Ruins. Garadar’s wanted notice associates the reavers with attacks on Garadar and the deaths of many orcs; the notice offers a reward for Zorbo’s death or capture.
A hostile Windyreed scavenger of Nagrand that attacks when provoked.
A humanoid Windyreed Wretch of Nagrand that fights with spells.
Goretooth is a notable beast of Nagrand.
Kil'sorrow Spellbinders are humanoid spellcasters of the Kil'sorrow area who hurl Arcane Missiles.
Kil'sorrow Cultists are humanoid fighters of the Kil'sorrow area who sear minds with Mind Sear.
Kil'sorrow Deathsworn are humanoid fighters found in the Kil'sorrow and adjacent areas. When badly wounded, they fight on with Bloodthirst.
A Vir’aani raider found around Forge Camps in Nagrand, it fights with Sinister Strike.
A Vir’aani arcanist of the Forge Camps in Nagrand. It holds its ground outside combat, then uses its magic in battle.
A Gan’arg tinkerer at Nagrand’s forge camps, one of the engineers and tinkerers Altruis wants kept busy to slow the Legion’s work. It can unleash a spell when wounded.
A Felguard Legionnaire at Nagrand's forge camps, among the Legion forces Altruis wants hindered in their work on the transporters. It attacks with a fel spell.

A water spirit of Skysong Lake, agitated by a disturbance in Nagrand’s waters and causing destruction there. Elementalist Lo’ap asks that the spirits be dealt with while the disturbance’s source is pursued.
A muck spawn of Nagrand's lakes and marshes that hurls spells at intruders.
Lake Surgers inhabit Nagrand’s waters. Elementalist Lo’ap’s quest describes them as corrupt offspring created by Watoosun’s polluted essence and asks that eight be destroyed.
Tortured Earth Spirits are found across Nagrand; Gordawg wants them put to sleep once more. In combat they can become enraged, strike with Earth Shock, and fall into a frenzy when badly hurt.
Shattered Rumblers are found in Nagrand and shake the ground with Earth Rumble.
Dust Howlers roam Nagrand and unleash a spell as their health falls through a middle range.
Storm Ragers roam Nagrand and unleash a spell as their health falls through a middle range.
Living Cyclones roam Nagrand, renewing their Lightning Shield when it fades and pulling targets in range toward them with Magnetic Pull.

K'ure is a naaru trapped in the wreck of the draenei vessel Oshu'gun. He recalls its former place in draenei life and explains that his failing energy drew orc ancestral spirits into a void, causing their suffering. He directs the search for a way to free them to A'dal in Shattrath.
Voidspawn are hostile void creatures found near Oshu'gun. The crew at Aeris Landing regards them as a nearby danger, and these creatures attack with Mind Sear and Pain Spike.
Dark Worgs are hostile beasts found in the Nagrand area.
Warmaul Warlocks are spellcasters among the Warmaul attackers at Warmaul Hill. They can summon imps and were among the raiders who attacked Elder Yorley's procession.

Agitated Orc Spirits are restless undead manifestations found around the Ancestral Grounds. Mother Kashur explains that the apparitions are not the ancestors themselves, but representations of their agitated state; something has disturbed the normally quiet grounds, though its cause is not yet known.
Enraged Crushers are aggressive elementals found across Outland. They knock foes down, and when badly wounded they fly into a frenzy.

Garrosh Hellscream, son of Grom and chieftain of the Mag’har, fears that his bloodline is cursed and that he could repeat his father’s failure. Doubt in his fitness to lead can leave him ashamed to face Greatmother Geyah, yet he fiercely demands respect for her. He addresses Thrall with deference and can rally his people with the Hellscream battle cry.
A Warmaul shaman serving among the attackers at Warmaul Hill, this combatant is named as one of Zorbo the Advisor’s forces in the wanted notice against him.
A Warmaul brute at Warmaul Hill, counted among the attackers who ambushed Elder Yorley’s procession, killed guards and desecrated an elder’s remains.

Farseer of the Lightning Sons in Garadar, Kurkush urges resistance to the Murkblood after their raids and seizure of Sunspring Post. Their idols are to be brought to him so the Lightning Sons can strike back. He voices hope that an outsider may protect them while Garrosh is depressed and failing to lead.

Farseer of the Lightning Sons in Garadar, Corhuk asks for help finding younglings who left to fight the Murkblood after a raid. Later, he receives word that one has chosen not to return and accepts that decision with grief and spiritual resolve.

Farseer Margadesh is a leader of the Lightning Sons at Garadar. With Murkblood raiders threatening the orcs, he argues for targeting their leadership instead of killing indiscriminately. He asks for their leader Ortor’s head and says he will display it near Garadar’s gates as a warning to future attackers.

Mogor, the Warmaul Hero, is the Ring of Blood’s boastful ogre champion. He taunts challengers, mocks defeated opponents, and reacts with outrage when one defeats Skra’gath, insisting the challenger must face him. His threats and boasts are blunt and often stumble over difficult words; when the final contest begins, he promises to destroy his opponent.

Elementalist Untrag of the Earthen Ring studies a disturbance he feels beating beneath the earth at the Throne of the Elements. He says the repeated pounding is making the earth reel and that Gordawg knows what is forcing the elements out. Untrag directs others to listen to Gordawg for insight, and cautions visitors not to upset the elements.

Elementalist Sharvak serves the Earthen Ring at the Throne of the Elements in Nagrand, where she worries that turmoil in the elements leaves her people unable to fight and the world without their support. She regards a blood elf child’s visit as foolhardy, yet promises to keep Salandria safe and hopes exposure to the elements may teach her something.

Elementalist Lo’ap serves the Earthen Ring at the Throne of the Elements and works to heal Nagrand’s disturbed waters and restless spirits. He says with shame that his own kin are polluting the land, and the Ring takes no pride in destroying the agitated spirits but acts to heal the land. He also prepares a caracoli tablet to help visitors breathe underwater.

Elementalist Morgh is an Earthen Ring elementalist who studies threats to the elements. He recognizes the Howling Wind as a distress call from an outside force seeking to subvert them. After learning that Murkbloods are capturing air spirits and using them to sow chaos, he is troubled by their control of the elements and says he must consult the others. He also identifies the Murkblood as his kin, a Broken tribe serving Musel'ek.

Captain Kroghan commands Horde forces at Garadar and considers the Mag'har kin to all the Horde, whose people he is proud to defend. When reinforcements are urgently needed, he welcomes any able-bodied fighter or spellcaster who can help. Although his original orders were to stay briefly in Garadar and then report to Blood Guard Gulmok at Shadowmoon Village, Kroghan believes Garadar needs a long-term Horde liaison. He delays his report because he considers his mission there unfinished, and expects Gulmok to understand.

Nahuud welcomes visitors to Telaar who have earned the trust of his people. He says Ikuti is like a brother to him and treats Ikuti’s trusted friend as a friend of his own, thanking them for helping his people.

Gordawg speaks in short, simple phrases and reads the land through the earth itself. He asks that tortured earth spirits be put to sleep, tastes a rock to learn where it came from, and treats the poison in it as evidence of an usurper contaminating Nagrand.

Incineratus is the Fury of Fire. Elementalist Lo'ap says the living fire used against the Lost Ones was plucked from Incineratus's fiery essence, linking him to the elemental response to their spread.
Aborius is the Fury of Water.
Kalandrios is the Fury of Air.

Jorin Deadeye is a Mag’har survivor of the Boulderfist ogre attack on his village, now the Bleeding Hollow Ruins. He is the son of Kilrogg and the last of the Deadeye lineage. Jorin condemns Garrosh for refusing aid and urges resistance, sending help to the village and directing attacks meant to teach the Boulderfist a lesson. He also seeks a diplomatic withdrawal after learning their leader is an orc.
Living Fire is a living flame drawn from the essence of Incineratus and given to be unleashed on the huts at Windyreed Village. Its recorded cry is “Burn! Burn! Burn!”

Greatmother Geyah is a Mag'har elder in Garadar and the grandmother of Thrall, whom she recognizes as Go'el, son of Durotan and rightful chieftain of the Frostwolves. She welcomes the chance to tell Garrosh what she learned about his father, Grom, and urges Thrall to share that account with him. Her grief and joy show how the revelation of family history reaches beyond personal reunion to the Mag'har's painful past.

Hemet Nesingwary is an old, seasoned dwarf hunter who runs a safari in Nagrand. He makes aspiring hunters prove their skill against increasingly dangerous clefthoof, from the ordinary herd to bulls and the elusive Banthar. For Hemet, a successful hunt shows cunning and determination as well as nerve. When greeting a returning hunter, he recalls their shaky start in Stranglethorn and successful hunt for Bangalash, then warns that Outland's prey is the real deal—and says he has the scars to prove it.
A minion of Gurok, the usurper, in Nagrand. Gordawg wants such minions destroyed to uncover the truth about the poison rock.

Arechron speaks for his people at Telaar and answers threats against them. He recognizes Ortor as someone he once knew, now serving Musel'ek and directing an invasion, and wants him dead. Arechron calls Corki his son and says that, despite his foolishness, he is still his blood; Corki's repeated disappearances exasperate and embarrass him. He knows of a totem but says only the chosen may learn more.
A Horde guard serving among the Halaani force.

Shado “Fitz” Farstrider is a safari hunter who treats hunting as a test of skill and a way to understand one’s place in nature. He urges hunters to push their limits, progressing from ordinary windrocs to more dangerous prey and ultimately Gutripper. Fitz recounts meeting Hemet Nesingwary while stalking the same frostsaber in Winterspring; a wager over its skin cost him his nickname, a story he tells with evident embarrassment.

A Murkblood putrifier is one of the tribe’s agents in its campaign against the elemental spirits around Sunspring. Elementalist Morgh identifies the putrifiers as captors of air spirits whose use of elemental magic sows disorder among the elements.
A Murkblood raider is among the enemies at Sunspring Post whom the Mag’har seek help fighting. The raiders are named as a target in the plea for vengeance from a lone orc.
Arechron identifies Ortor as someone he once knew: a formerly noble Broken, versed in elemental ways, now described as a muck-addled follower of Musel'ek. The quest points to Ortor at Sunspring.
One of the Murkblood scavengers named among the enemies at Sunspring Post, where Arechron directs his call for vengeance.

A Kurenai captive held by Murkblood searching for the totem of Kar'dash and questioning Kurenai about it. During the escape, the captive warns of an ambush and pursuers, then proposes splitting up near the road to Telaar so one of them may reach safety and report to Arechron.

The Mag'har captive was kidnapped by Murkbloods during a nighttime raid on Garadar and learned they sought the Totem of Kar'dash. During his escape, he warns of pursuers and casts lightning and frost shock. If he cannot return, he asks that Garrosh be told what happened.
A Murkblood pursuer taking part in the attack on the captive, the brute urges the others to stop the escape and kill the strong one first.

Harold Lane is a hunter at the Nesingwary Safari, laid up by an infected thorn scratch from a fight with a talbuk stag and an attack by windroc hunters, whose beaks he keeps as trophies. Coughing and in pain, he asks others to hunt talbuk in his place: first stags, then tougher thorngrazers, and finally Bach'lor, the great stag. He cares most about finishing the hunt despite being temporarily laid up.
Ravenous windrocs are deadly flying predators hunted as challenging prey in Nagrand. Their attacks can threaten hunters pursuing talbuk; the windrocs’ beaks are kept as trophies.

At Telaar, Otonbu treats the Sunspring deaths as both a public-health danger and a threat to peace with the orcs. He considers burning the bodies a grim necessity to protect the water and both peoples, while recognizing the act will set reconciliation back.

Mo'mor directs Telaar's response to the Boulderfist threat, which he sees as a possible prelude to invasion. After the town's recent recovery, he presses attacks on ogre groups, weighs reports about the Warmaul tribe, and also sends an envoy to seek the Boulderfist leader's cooperation.

At Telaar, Poli'lukluk connects the Murkblood's violence with Nagrand's disturbed elementals and wildlife, and with renewed orc hostility toward the Kurenai. He stresses that orcs may mistake all Broken for the Murkblood and urges resolving the violence without treating the tribes as one people.
A talbuk patriarch, a mature male talbuk of Nagrand.

Saurfang the Younger recounts being the last survivor of a Murkblood attack on his war party and experiencing a consuming rage he cannot explain. He seeks blood-for-blood vengeance but feels shame at asking a stranger for help. He believes a greater purpose awaits him beyond Garadar and asks that Farseer Corhuk be told of his wish to walk the earth.

Ioki is an Earthen Ring elementalist visiting Telaar to report the state of the elements to the Kurenai. Ioki asks a traveler to tell Sharvak at the Throne of the Elements that the visit has gone safely.

Yal'hah is an Earthen Ring elementalist visiting Garadar to report the state of the elements to the Mag'har. Yal'hah asks a traveler to tell Sharvak at the Throne of the Elements that the visit has gone safely.
A Murkblood tribal fighter associated with the assaults on Garadar. It often carries a Murkblood Idol, the kind Farseer Kurkush wants brought to him.
An Alliance Halaani Guard, a member of the Alliance guard force associated with Halaa.

Gutripper is a singular female windroc, called the mother of the greater windrocs, found among them far to the west in Nagrand. Fitz at the Nesingwary Safari treats facing her as a hunter's test of honor, and Hemet counts her as nothing next to Tusker.

Bach'lor is a singular male stag called king of the stags, found leading his herd in western Nagrand. Harold Lane wants one of his hooves as proof of a hunt, and Hemet counts Bach'lor among the named Nagrand beasts overshadowed by Tusker.

Banthar is a singular female clefthoof, described by Hemet Nesingwary as the fiercest and most elusive of her kind, as well as exceptionally hairy. She roams with a clefthoof herd in the Field of Spirits near Oshu'gun; Hemet counts her as nothing next to Tusker.

Lantresor of the Blade is a calculating leader who plans to turn the Kil'sorrow and Warmaul against each other. He has others stage evidence of attacks, planting Warmaul banners among fallen Kil'sorrow and using smoke to signal his ogres to place bodies. His plan aims to win back Boulderfist territory and free those he speaks to from attacks by the rival groups and the Shadow Council. His greeting is measured and threatening: a dangerous strategist whose negotiations serve a wider political purpose.

Gezhe represents the Consortium at Aeris Landing in Nagrand. He says Nexus-Prince Haramad halted the planned Oshu'gun excavation pending a political matter in Netherstorm, so he redirected the operation toward smuggled gems. Gezhe treats fragments taken by Gava'xi's band as Consortium property, while admitting that claim is technically premature. With excavation on hold, he also turns obsidian warbeads from Nagrand ogres into another source of income and offers gems to Consortium associates in return for loyalty.
A Consortium gemcutter in Nagrand.
A Consortium overseer in Nagrand.

Zerid is the security officer overseeing the safety of Gezhe’s operation near Oshu’gun. He regards the nearby voidspawn and rogue ethereals, especially their leader Gava’xi, as threats to the crew and makes neutralizing them a priority. He dryly notes that Gezhe chose the risky site for a projected productivity gain while leaving security to him, and jokes that his security budget is small.

Pilot Marsha is an engineer who is repairing her crashed aircraft. She blames Hemet’s habit of shooting through its ailerons while hunting for the crash, but says she expects to have the aircraft fixed quickly.
Tusker, styled Queen of the Elekk, is a giant female elekk feared in Nagrand, far larger than any ordinary elekk. Hemet Nesingwary ranks her above Bach'lor, Gutripper and Banthar.
A Bleeding Hollow Refugee is a spectator who cheers for the pitfighter, praises his discipline, and marvels at his skill.
A Sunspring Post refugee watching the pitfighter, this spectator admires his discipline and wonders at his skill. The refugee expects him to win.

Kristen Dipswitch collected skins in Zangarmarsh and has a bundle for Harold Lane at the Nesingwary Safari. If rescued from Gankly Rottenfist, she is glad to have escaped his ruthless grasp. She greets Harold with news that she has his skins.
A Sunspring Post orphan watching the pitfighter, this young spectator marvels at his muscles and hopes to grow up like him. The child wonders whether the fighter will win.

Gava'xi is a rogue ethereal leader whom Zerid identifies as a dangerous criminal and threat to the operations near Oshu'gun. Zerid has made neutralizing him a priority and calls for his defeat. Gava'xi fights with strikes and gouges.
A Bleeding Hollow orphan in Nagrand.

Elkay'gan the Mystic is a Mag'har quest giver in Garadar. He asks for battle standards to be placed at three Burning Blade pyres in the ogre compound, hoping to leave a lasting impression on the ogres. He also seeks the return of supplies stolen from the village; recovering them would ease the burden on Garadar's matrons. His reward dialogue acknowledges that the Mag'har have little left after the attacks.

Matron Celestine is a Mag'har quest giver in Garadar. She recounts that Altruis arrived on a nether drake, asked questions about Nagrand, and said he hunted the Legion. Before leaving, he asked the people of Garadar to direct would-be heroes to him in western Nagrand, where he expected to stay for a while.

Matron Drakia is a Mag'har matron in Garadar, responsible for many local matters. With Greatmother ill, Drakia asks for help finding a funeral procession that left several days earlier for the Ancestral Grounds. She says Greatmother raised all the Mag'hari and that her life, like theirs, was touched by her; she also recalls Greatmother urging them to serve their people and show Garrosh that life goes on.

Shadrek is an ivory trader at Aeris Landing who offers suppliers a share of the profits from wild elekk tusks, claiming he has an understanding with both the orcs and draenei. He is hard-nosed about the bargain: he rejects excuses and raises renegotiation when a supplier falls short. He later says his budget can no longer cover a profit share, while continued supply may earn the supplier standing with the Consortium.
Wild elekks roam Nagrand and are prized for their high-quality ivory tusks. Shadrek, who trades in ivory, wants wild elekk tusks and considers bull elekk ivory unsuitable.

A Consortium recruiter presenting the ethereal organization as honest, industrious and pleasant, while candidly asking for loyalty, dedication and moral flexibility. The recruiter frames contact as mutual assistance and directs interested visitors to Gezhe, the Consortium's ground-operations leader at Aeris Landing.
A Consortium claviger in Nagrand.

Lump is an ogre whom Bintook identifies as a possible source of information about an ogre lieutenant's battle plans. He says he is hungry, jokes that people are food in Nagrand, and expresses willingness to give up; he is threatening but willing to yield.

A Boulderfist hunter is one of the ogres in the hunting party camped east of Telaar. Bintook sees the group as a new threat to Nagrand alongside the Murkbloods; these hunters are part of the force whose plans she wants investigated.

Huntress Bintook is a Telaar huntress worried that ogres have appeared east of town after the Murkblood threat, with too few people to answer every danger. She wants the ogre hunting party investigated, reads their plans with baffled uncertainty about their meaning, and urges that Mo'mor be told exactly what the ogre said.

Corki is a captive of the Boulderfist ogres, frightened they will eat him. He asks to be freed and directs his rescuer to search the ogres for a key. Corki says his father, Arechron, leads Telaar and will reward whoever gets him out; he also thanks a rescuer and says his father will reward them before saying goodbye.

Giselda the Crone is a Kil'sorrow figure wanted by the wardens of Garadar and Telaar. Their notices accuse her and her lackeys of murder, ritual sacrifice, communing with the Legion, kidnapping and burglary, and place them at Kil'sorrow Fortress. In combat she threatens to coat the fortress walls with her enemy's blood, casts Mind Sear and transforms as her health falls.

Warden Bullrok is Garadar’s warden, focused on protecting its people from Nagrand’s threats. His words convey alarm over repeated ogre kidnappings, and he directs visitors seeking work to the bulletin board. His assignments address threats such as the crone and Durn the Hungerer, while he also invites people to prove their strength against ogres; his remarks emphasize the danger and the rewards Garadar can offer.

Warden Moi'bff Jill helps meet Telaar's needs by rallying adventurers to its work board and asking allies to prove loyalty with warbeads taken from Nagrand's ogres. She says she was once called Iolol, until a secret town vote forced her to change her name; she jokes that the alternative was ending up like Corki and calls her new name a huge improvement.

Durn the Hungerer, called the Son of Gruul, is a gronn who lords over the Spirit Fields around Oshu'gun. A wanted quest handled by Warden Moi'bff Jill describes him as a ferocious threat who has devastated Nagrand and remained beyond the reach of those trying to stop him.

Zorbo the Advisor is a Warmaul threat based in the Laughing Skull Ruins of northern Nagrand. Wanted posters name him with Warmaul shamans and reavers, describe him as armed, dangerous and merciless, and offer a reward for his death or capture.

Elder Yorley is one of only two survivors of a thirty-orc Mag'hari funeral procession ambushed on its way to the Ancestral Grounds. The attack killed guards and desecrated an elder's remains. A spiritual orc, Yorley nevertheless calls for retribution against the Warmaul attackers and their leader, Cho'war, to defend the Mag'hari dead and sacred rites.

Elder Ungriz is one of only two survivors of the Mag'hari funeral procession ambushed by Warmaul. He urges a search for survivors and believes the captured Mag'har may still be alive, asking that they be brought back alive. When they return, Ungriz calls their rescue an achievement no one thought possible and names their rescuer a hero to the Mag'har.

Huntress Kima survived a Warmaul ogre attack on her supply caravan, escaped captivity, and wants the stolen crates recovered. She also recalls Altruis visiting and asking about Nagrand before continuing his hunt for the Legion. Kima regrets telling Arechron’s son Corki what happened; he has gone missing again.

Altruis is a demon hunter who still respects Illidan, but now believes power and defeat have corrupted him and vows to destroy what he has become. He hunts demons regardless of their allegiance and gathers intelligence to strike the Legion. Altruis is wary of corruption in himself, too: a book's promise of power tempts him, and he begs someone to take it from him before it sways his will, to use against Varedis.
Nethrandamus is the escort Altruis trusts to carry an observer over Legion camps and keep them safe while they catalog the camps' structures and defenses for his intelligence gathering.

Cho'war is the Warmaul ogre king who drove the gronn from their cave and broke up the clans that had served them. Corki describes him as powerful and says he lives in the big cave, while Elder Yorley identifies him as the ruler who made Warmaul.

A captive Mag'har held by the ogres at Warmaul Hill, one among many prisoners there. Their brief words range from defiance and gratitude to hope that a hero will lift the orcs toward their former glory.

Garokk, the Ring of Trials' former battlemaster, remembers it as a place of great glory and honor before the Steamwheedle Cartel arrived with wagons of gold and quill pens sharper than an orc axe. His words preserve his view of the ring's changed order.

Bufferlo is a Warmaul ogre cook whose threats make Corki the promised ingredient in his stew. He barks cooking commands, briefly jokes that Corki's father might pay for him, then says the ogres will eat him anyway.

Corki is Arechron's son and a captive of the Warmaul ogres, with Cho'war holding his cage key. His father considers him foolish but still wants him saved. Corki asks for the key, expects his father to reward a rescue, and after repeated rescues warmly declares the rescuer blood family in his own reckoning.

Gurgthock promotes and announces bouts in the Ring of Blood, testing challengers against Brokentoe, the Murkblood twins and eventually Mogor. He warns that fights end with one side down, recommends bringing friends and allows a hesitant challenger to back out. The bouts make him considerable money, and he tempts a champion with a full-time gladiator partnership promising a mountain of gold. Rewards are collected from Wodin the Troll-Servant.
A Telaari watcher in Nagrand.

A Garadar defender whose remarks reveal the community's awe at Thrall's return: one feels ready to give their life for him, while others wonder who he is and ask whether he carries the Greatmother's bloodline.
Demos is a demon, the Overseer of Hate at Forge Camp: Hate.
Xirkos is a demon, the Overseer of Fear at Forge Camp: Fear.

The Mo'arg Master Planner is associated with the forge camps, where planners determine the structures and their arrangement. Altruis's quest describes recovering this planner's blueprints from behind the forges.
A Kil'sorrow ritualist who stands its ground and fights with Shadow Bolt and Corruption.
Subjugator Vaz'shir is a lone demon subjugator in Nagrand who casts spells in battle.
A Terrorguard casts two spells, one when engaged and another within a particular health range.
An Orc Ancestor.
Voidhunter Yar is a demon who taunts victims that in the void no one can hear their screams. It absorbs holy and fire energy from attacks, and strikes with Shadow Bolt and Holy Smite.
Bro'Gaz the Clanless is a humanoid found in Nagrand.

Mother Kashur seeks serenity for Nagrand's ancestors and safety for the Mag'har, investigating the spirits' agitation and departure from their villages. Kashur explains that the hostile ghosts represent the ancestors' troubled state rather than being the ancestors themselves. Oshu'gun is remembered as a sacred gathering place whose spirits fell silent when the clans became a horde. Kashur sends an investigator there to discover what now draws the spirits from rest and expresses profound gratitude for aid.
Ancient orc ancestors invoke ancestral protection for kind visitors but also cry out in torment, describing spirits calling and a sense of being consumed.
Furgu is the hippogryph master in Nagrand, who flies travelers by hippogryph. When attacked, he calls for guards and summons an enraged hippogryph.
Gursha is the wind rider master in Nagrand, who flies travelers by wind rider. When attacked, she calls for guards and summons an enraged wyvern.

Chief Researcher Amereldine leads research at Halaa into the naaru crystals associated with Oshu'gun. She seeks recurring samples of crystal powder and offers compensation for contributions. Her words frame the work as part of the fight against the Alliance in Outland.

Chief Researcher Kartos leads research at Halaa into the naaru crystals associated with Oshu'gun. He seeks recurring samples of crystal powder and offers compensation for contributions. His words frame the work as part of the fight against the Horde in Outland.
Quartermaster Jaffrey Noreliqe is a quartermaster who offers goods for sale in Halaa, Nagrand.
Quartermaster Davian Vaclav sells goods for Halaa tokens of battle and research.

Ear-Biter is the Steamwheedle Fighting Circuit arena battlemaster. His dialogue brusquely challenges would-be fighters while also dismissing some applicants as unfit, giving him a sharp, confrontational manner at the arena.

“King” Dond organizes the Steamwheedle Fighting Circuit and sells arena team charters for ranked matches. He welcomes visitors to the stadium with pointed sarcasm about its recent appropriation and renaming, and is blunt with those he judges unfit to fight.
Matron Tikkit is Garadar’s innkeeper, offering travelers a place to rest and goods for sale. She also lets guests make the inn their home.

Caregiver Isel is an innkeeper who welcomes guests to sit and get comfortable. She offers goods for sale and lets visitors make the inn their home; during the Hallow’s End interaction, she can also respond to a trick-or-treat greeting.
An injured talbuk.

Osrok the Immovable is an armorsmith and blacksmithing supplies merchant. He offers repairs, framing the need for sharp blades and reinforced armor as part of restoring tranquility to Nagrand and meting out justice.

Sparik is an armorsmith and blacksmithing supplies merchant who offers repairs. His repair greeting links sharp blades and reinforced armor with restoring tranquility to Nagrand and meting out justice.
Vanteg sells reagents and poison supplies in the town.
Ogir sells reagents and poison supplies. He asks visitors whether they are looking for either, and offers his wares.
Mathar G'ochar sells trade supplies in the town.
Borto sells trade supplies: wares that crafters need, just the basics, nothing fancy.
Wilda Bearmane is a stable master who offers help stabling pets and recovering lost companions.
Luftasia is a stable master in the town. She can point visitors toward the vendors near its center.
Matron Qualia is a general-goods seller in the area. Her services also include ammunition.
Nancila sells general goods in the area. She describes her stock as “odds and ends, but mostly just odds,” giving her shop a wryly self-deprecating touch.
A panther kept in the local stable, one of several stabled animals in the area.
A tallstrider kept in the local stable, identified among the stabled animals in the area.
A boar kept in the local stable, one of the animals present among the local stable’s occupants.
A bear kept in the local stable; this stabled animal is identified separately from the nearby panther, tallstrider, and boar.
A raptor kept in a stable in Nagrand.
A Kurenai lion kept in a stable in Nagrand.
A Kurenai panther kept in a stable in Nagrand.

Wazat is preoccupied with obtaining eggs and getting his Jump-a-tron 4000 working. He recruits help gathering air elemental gas, then asks for an egg from a nearby nest using the machine. His remarks dwell on the eggs, and he warns that the jump can cause serious injury; after receiving the machine parts, he gives the helper a key while noting that the device still needs adjustments.
The Jump-a-tron 4000 is a named mechanical device in Nagrand.
A wolf rider of Garadar in Nagrand.
An elekk rider of the Telaari in Nagrand.

Ohlorn Farstrider calls himself a hunter extraordinaire and a member of the Nesingwary expedition, which came from Azeroth to hunt big game. He says Nagrand's untamed plains offer some of his best hunting, and directs interested hunters toward his crew at the Nesingwary Safari.

"Shotgun" Jones recounts being sent to find supplies and nearly killed repeatedly before reaching the Broken. He says he will not return to big-game hunting, has quit the Nesingwary Safari, and warns that the Broken may be dangerous to face.
The Nagrand Target Dummy serves as a practice target.
The Mag'har Pitfighter is a pit fighter in Nagrand who fights with his fists.

A Kurenai pitfighter needles visitors about whether they are tough enough for the Ring of Blood, then points them toward Gurgthock, who runs the fights and awards prizes. His teasing challenge is an invitation to prove oneself.
A captured Halaani blood knight, one of several held in the Halaa area.
Interrogator Khan serves with the Hand of Argus.

A Telaari jailor who relays what he has heard about the blood elves' purpose in Nagrand and urges allies to join the fighting at Halaa. He presents the claim about Oshu'gun's crystal residue as rumor and calls the blood elves' intentions insidious.
A captured Halaani vindicator, one of several held in the Halaa area.

A Garadar guard captain who reports a scout's account of draenei attacking two wolf riders and says Garadar won the skirmish. He strongly hates draenei, even more than blood elves, and urges visitors to attack draenei and their allies at Halaa.
Mountain Gronn are gronn that live in Nagrand.

The Fel Cannon: Fear is a weapon at Forge Camp: Fear. It projects a fel energy beam at a nearby target and can be turned and fired at the camp as part of Altruis the Sufferer's task to destroy the camp.

D'ore is a weakened naaru spirit whose remains were brought to Auchindoun by the Prophet Velen and his draenei companions after a crash. Laid to rest in a sarcophagus, D'ore has spent nearly a thousand years regenerating. D'ore describes the darkened essence as part of the naaru's cycle of Light and void.

The Consortium Nether Runner reports to Gezhe, addressing him as “sir” and bringing news from the Hara'samid Sector. Its reports mention a collapse in heavy veldarite markets that Gezhe predicted, rising Heraazi exports, bribes to taxation officers, and contraband expected within days. Its deferential parting, “By your leave, sir,” reinforces its subordinate role.

Nitrin the Learned is a scholar of death lore at the Abandoned Armory in Nagrand who works against Levixus and his threat to Auchindoun. He brews a tincture that lets the drinker see the spirit world, admitting the effect is permanent and that many initiates go mad. He urges haste, as Levixus's army grows.
A cobalt war talbuk, a friendly animal.
Uriku is a cooking-supplies merchant in Nagrand.
Nula the Butcher is a cooking-supplies merchant in Nagrand.
Trader Narasu serves as the Kurenai quartermaster in Nagrand. His title marks his role supplying the Kurenai; he is distinct from the Mag'har quartermaster.
Provisioner Nasela is the Mag'har quartermaster in Nagrand. Her title identifies her as a supplier for the Mag'har, distinct from Kurenai quartermaster Trader Narasu.

Corki is Arechron's curious son, whose urge to investigate trouble has repeatedly landed him in danger. After being rescued from the Burning Blade Ruins, he set out to investigate the Boulderfist ogres for Mo'mor and was caught again; when freed, he promises this will be the last time.
Coreiel is a blade merchant in Nagrand, serving travelers who need weapons and repairs.
Tasaldan supplies ammunition in the Halaani Basin area of Nagrand. His focused trade complements the nearby blade merchant Coreiel, giving armed travelers another kind of practical supply.
Embelar is a food-and-drink merchant.
Aldraan is a blade merchant who offers goods to browse.
Cendrii is a food-and-drink merchant who offers goods to browse.
Banro is an ammunition merchant who offers goods to browse.
The Avatar of Sathal is a demoness who can take incorporeal form and watches over the wrath priestesses at Forge Base: Gehenna. When confronted, she threatens her attacker.

npcs.name: Air Force Guard Post (Horde - Bat Rider)

records.text: A Horde air force guard post associated with bat riders.
A Horde rooftop trip wire deployed across the air force’s Netherstorm sites.
An elemental creature called a Crashing Wave-Spirit, found in Netherstorm’s Eco-Dome Midrealm.
An elemental creature called a Storming Wind-Ripper, found in Netherstorm’s Eco-Dome Midrealm.
An elemental creature called a Raging Fire-Soul, found in Netherstorm’s Eco-Dome Midrealm.
An elemental creature called a Rumbling Earth-Heart, found in Netherstorm’s Eco-Dome Midrealm.
A Deathshadow acolyte, a spellcaster who scorches its enemies with Mind Sear.
A Deathshadow spellbinder, a spellcaster who channels a purple beam of magic when not fighting.
A Deathshadow archon who fights with Bloodthirst and flies into a rage when badly wounded.

Reth'hedron the Subduer is identified by Illidari Lord Balthas as his brother. Balthas says the same blood flows through them and calls Reth'hedron's allegiance misplaced; he asks that Reth'hedron be subdued with a soul cannon attuned to that blood. The quest presents their kinship and divided allegiance as central to the conflict.
A Deathshadow warlock, a spellcaster who wards itself with Demon Armor when not fighting.
A Deathshadow overlord who hurls fireballs at its foes.

Jheel is an apprentice at Aeris Landing, learning gemcutting under Gezhe. He is interested in geology and misses his younger sister, Dornaa, while away from her. His gemcutting exams are a step toward visiting the orphanage again.

Wodin handles the Ring of Blood bouts and lines up the next match. He acknowledges a fighter's success, but admits he takes a cut from the championship and wants the ogres kept unaware of the arrangement.
Elaira is still earning the sparrowhawks' trust. She gently reassures them, then trains a captured hawk to help find pieces of the Book of the Raven and promises it will be free after the task.
Paulsta'ats is the Consortium Quartermaster, a merchant who also repairs gear.
A wild twilight serpent of Nagrand.
Challe is a named individual who asks others to keep their voices down because the babes are sleeping. This suggests a quiet, protective concern for the sleeping young.
Jara is a humanoid in Nagrand.
Chaddo is a humanoid in Nagrand.
Sa'rah is a humanoid in Nagrand.
Seer Nakha describes a vision of an immense arrow rising on a trail of fire, a feat he says is not magical. He urges help for the people working on it, whose efforts may fail without more hands.

Seer Jovar’s visions include a fire-trailing cloud tied to a distant creation and green fire falling on Wildhammer defenders in Shadowmoon Valley. He presents these visions as warnings and urges help for those facing danger.

Lakoor says his people do not seek war but will defend their lands. He fears a Horde victory in Halaa, questions what the blood elves are scheming, and points to a history of bloodshed and betrayal between his people and the orcs.

Karrtog regards the draenei as an ancient enemy and fears that their side’s victory in Halaa would put Garadar next in danger. He describes his people as few in number and the draenei’s return as a serious concern.
Grikkin Copperspring is an arena merchant in Nagrand.
The Nagrand Flame Warden welcomes visitors to the Alliance fire, urging them to honor Alliance flames and desecrate Horde fires.
The Nagrand Flame Keeper welcomes visitors to the Horde fire, urging them to honor Horde flames and desecrate Alliance fires.

place_records.text: You are in Nagrand, a contested part of Outland where the Alliance and the Horde both hold settlements. Garadar is Horde, Telaar is Alliance, and the abandoned city of Halaa belongs to neither side. Ogres are the main danger, from Boulderfist and Warmaul ogres to the Murkblood who sacked Sunspring Post. Legion forge camps, rumblers, clefthoofs and windrocs also roam the plains.

You are in Burning Blade Ruins, a ruin in Nagrand where Boulderfist mystics and crushers roam. Lantresor of the Burning Blade is a calculating leader who schemes to turn the Kil'sorrow and the Warmaul against each other. Corki, son of Arechron, is held captive by the Boulderfist ogres here.

You are in Garadar, the Mag'har town in Nagrand held by the Horde. Chieftain Garrosh Hellscream, son of Grom, fears his cursed bloodline and doubts his fitness to lead, while Greatmother Geyah, an elder, keeps watch over the town. Farseer Kurkush of the Lightning Sons presses resistance against the Murkblood raiders who took Sunspring Post. Its flight master and inn serve travelers.
You are in Skysong Lake, a lake in Nagrand where the water spirits have been agitated. Lake spirits roam its waters, and a goretooth lurks here among them.

You are in Throne of the Elements, the Earthen Ring's seat in Nagrand, held by the Alliance. Elementalists Sharvak, Lo'ap and Untrag work here to calm the disturbed elements, and Gordawg, Fury of Earth, reads the land through the earth itself. Untrag says a pounding beneath the ground is making the earth reel, and Sharvak worries that her people cannot fight while the elements are in turmoil.
You are in Laughing Skull Ruins, a Warmaul ogre site in Nagrand. Warmaul reavers and shamans hold the ruins, and Zorbo the Advisor is among the ogres here.

You are in Warmaul Hill, a Warmaul ogre hill in Nagrand where many prisoners are kept. Corki, son of Arechron, is caged here, and Cho'war holds the key to his cage. Warmaul warlocks, brutes and a chef named Bufferlo guard the hill, and a Mag'har captive is among the prisoners.

You are in Lake Sunspring, the region's main water source in Nagrand. Lake surgers and Watoosun's Polluted Essence roam its waters, and the Murkblood have begun dumping the slain from Sunspring Post into it.

You are in Sunspring Post, a fishing village in Nagrand that the Murkblood drove its orcs out of. Murkblood raiders, brutes and Ortor of the Murkblood still hold the post, and captives from the Kurenai and the Mag'har have been held here while the Murkblood search for the totem of Kar'dash.

You are in Aeris Landing, a Consortium outpost in Nagrand. Gezhe represents the Consortium here and has turned the Oshu'gun operation toward smuggled gems, while his security officer Zerid treats the voidspawn and the rogue ethereals led by the thief Gava'xi as threats. Shadrek trades in wild elekk ivory, and the outpost offers repairs and a vendor.

You are in Forge Camp: Fear, a Legion camp in Nagrand. Gan'arg tinkerers, Mo'arg engineers and Felguard legionnaires work here around the fel cannons, and Xirkos, Overseer of Fear, commands the camp. The overseers are extremely dangerous.

You are in Forge Camp: Hate, a Legion camp in Nagrand with fel cannons and the same mix of tinkerers, engineers and legionnaires as the camp of Fear. Demos, Overseer of Hate, leads them, and wild elekks wander nearby.

You are in Telaar, the Alliance town in Nagrand, led by Arechron. Mo'mor the Breaker directs the response to the Boulderfist threat, and Huntress Bintook worries that ogres have appeared east of town with too few people to answer every danger. Its inn and flight master serve travelers.

You are in Northwind Cleft, a cleft in Nagrand where Boulderfist warriors, Boulderfist mages and enraged crushers roam. Corki, Arechron's curious son, is an Alliance man who keeps getting caught up in trouble with the Boulderfist ogres. A spirit healer offers a return to life for a price.

You are in Halaa, a draenei research base in Nagrand that belongs to neither side, though Horde and Alliance both keep people here. Chief Researcher Amereldine for the Horde and Chief Researcher Kartos for the Alliance each study the naaru crystals of Oshu'gun and want samples of its crystal powder. Its vendors, repairs and a spirit healer serve travelers, though muck creatures roam the area.
You are in Southwind Cleft, a cleft in Nagrand where Boulderfist warriors, Boulderfist mages and enraged crushers roam.

You are in Oshu'gun, a mountain of crystal in Nagrand. Ancient orc ancestors here offer protection to kind visitors, yet they cry out in torment. Vir'aani raiders and arcanists, Terrorguards, Kil'sorrow ritualists and void creatures make the mountain dangerous.

You are in Spirit Fields, a part of Nagrand where K'ure, a naaru trapped in the wreck of the draenei vessel Oshu'gun, speaks to visitors. He explains that his failing energy drew orc ancestral spirits into a void, and he is still searching for a way to free them. Void creatures, Vir'aani raiders and arcanists, and Kil'sorrow ritualists make the fields dangerous.

You are in Ancestral Grounds, one of the villages of the orc ancestors in Nagrand, where Mother Kashur, a Horde figure, seeks peace for the spirits and safety for the Mag'har. Agitated orc spirits walk the grounds, and Kashur explains they are the ancestors' troubled state rather than the ancestors themselves.

You are in Windyreed Village, a village in Nagrand where Living Fire, a flame drawn from the essence of Incineratus, is set loose on the huts. Windyreed scavengers and wretches are the other troubles here.

You are in Elemental Plateau, a part of Nagrand where raging fire-souls, crashing wave-spirits, storming wind-rippers and rumbling earth-hearts roam. A spirit healer offers a return to life for a price.
You are in Kil'sorrow Fortress, a stronghold in Nagrand held by Kil'sorrow deathsworn, cultists and spellbinders, with dark worgs roaming nearby. Giselda the Crone is a notable foe here.

You are in The Ring of Trials, an arena in Nagrand that the Steamwheedle Fighting Circuit now runs. Garokk, its former master, remembers the ring's glory before the Steamwheedle Cartel arrived. Ear-Biter challenges would-be fighters, and King Dond organizes the circuit and sells charters for arena teams.
You are in Halaani Basin, a basin in Nagrand where muck creatures and enraged crushers roam, and Goretooth is among the dangers.

You are in Mag'hari Procession, a stretch of Nagrand where Horde Mag'har grieve. Elder Yorley and Elder Ungriz are two survivors of a thirty-orc funeral procession ambushed by Warmaul on its way to the Ancestral Grounds. Saurfang the Younger, the last survivor of a Murkblood attack on his war party, is consumed by a rage he cannot explain.

You are in Nesingwary Safari in Nagrand, a hunting safari run by Hemet Nesingwary, an old dwarf hunter. He makes aspiring hunters prove themselves against clefthoof, from the ordinary herd up to bulls and the elusive Banthar. Pilot Marsha is repairing her crashed aircraft here, blaming Hemet for shooting through its ailerons. Tortured earth spirits roam the area.

You are in the Ring of Blood in Nagrand, an arena where ogres stage fights. Gurgthock announces the bouts, and Mogor, the Warmaul Hero, is the boastful ogre champion who taunts fighters. Wodin the Troll-Servant lines up the next match and takes a cut of the championship.
You are in Telaari Basin in Nagrand, where wild elekks roam and are sought for their high-quality ivory tusks. Tortured earth spirits and enraged crushers roam here too.
You are in Windyreed Pass in Nagrand. Kristen Dipswitch is here, carrying a bundle of skins she collected in Zangarmarsh for Harold Lane at the Nesingwary Safari.

You are in The Twilight Ridge in Nagrand, where most of the sparrowhawks nest. Watcher Elaira is training a captured sparrowhawk to find pieces of the Book of the Raven. The spirit healer here offers a return to life for a price. Deathshadow spellbinders, warlocks and archons haunt the ridge.

You are in the Abandoned Armory in Nagrand. Nitrin the Learned works here against Levixus, the Soul Caller who threatens Auchindoun and binds the dead to his will. Boulderfist mages and warriors roam the area.
